title: E. Is this Segment Tree Beats?

legend: Tortles recently learned about segment tree beats, which is a segment tree modification that supports range ckmin and ckmax operations in amortizedO(logn2)$$$O(\log{n^2})$$$. Tortles decided to play with this funny data structure.

He started with an array a$$$a$$$ of n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ where (1≤ai≤10$$$1 \le a_i \le 10$$$). He then performed a series of operations over the entire array. In each operation, he chose a number x$$$x$$$ between 1$$$1$$$ and 10$$$10$$$ and either the operation min$$$min$$$ or max$$$max$$$. He then set each element ai$$$a_i$$$ to op(ai,x)$$$op(a_i, x)$$$ where op$$$op$$$ is the operation he chose.

Unfortunately, after he played around with the array, his computer crashed and he lost his edit history. Given the final array after all operations he performed, how many distinct possibilities are there for the original array a$$$a$$$?
input: The first line will have an integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤104$$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases.
The first line of each test case contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤9$$$1 \le n \le 9$$$) — the length of the array.

The second line of each test case contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ (1≤ai≤10$$$1 \le a_i \le 10$$$) — the values of the final array after all modifications are performed.
output: For each test case, print the number of possible starting arrays.
